title: Older and Wiser: The Marriage of Device Aging and Intellectual Property Protection of DNNs
problem: Deep neural networks like GPT-3 are kept secret due to high training costs and privacy concerns, but existing IP protection approaches require expensive circuit redesign that incurs significant area, energy, and latency overheads. There is a need for lightweight DNN IP protection without substantial hardware modification costs.
motivation: DNN models represent valuable intellectual property assets with billion-dollar training costs, making protection against model theft and unauthorized deployment critical for commercial viability.
method: The paper proposes a hardware-software co-design approach that exploits inherent device aging characteristics—the natural performance degradation of circuits over time—as a built-in protection mechanism. Differential orientation fine-tuning (DOFT) is introduced to ensure effective DNN protection while leveraging this aging phenomenon without requiring expensive circuit redesigns.
key_novelty: Using natural device aging as an intrinsic, zero-overhead IP protection mechanism for DNNs, combined with DOFT for effective security without circuit redesign.
contributions: Novel approach exploiting device aging characteristics for DNN IP protection
Differential orientation fine-tuning (DOFT) technique for protection
Hardware-software co-design eliminating expensive circuit redesign
Reduced area, energy, and latency overhead compared to prior protection schemes
